items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he sent me tons of Art Tatum‟s [records]

ctx.x: I know that you mentioned, you know, the lineage of Teddy Wilson and Bud Powell. What about Art Tatum? Does he figure in?

Art Tatum was something that was … when Norman Granz, after recording, he went back to the States and he sent me tons of Art Tatum‟s [records], because he recorded for [Granz], so he sent them to me. And … his recording … actually, frankly speaking, I neglected to say, but I heard his record before that, playing, uh, “Begin the Beguine.” And, uh, I think it was, I heard it at a jazz coffee shop, and it was really amazing technique, the way … and I think I sort of was…. But also, I heard “Elegy.” This is a…

like that, [so] Tatum must have been really great. I didn‟t get to hear him in person. But most recordings, it was really … I was amazed [at] his ability, and he would play one after another, and if I know Norman Granz, he probably didn‟t have a take two, everything blah, blah, blah, and it was so many standard tunes and so on. But, it didn‟t really hit my heart. The one who hit [my] heart was Bud Powell. He was the one, you know, who really hit my heart. He not only had enormous technique—later I learned that he…
